en: He, then drawing the string to his ears, shot many burning and deadly arrows thereby striking Karna in all his vital points, but Karna of great patience, though, he felt very painful, kept his face summoning all his courage.

sa: स्त्रियस्त्वाशङ्किताः पापा नोपगम्या विजानता। रजसा ता विशुध्यन्ते भस्मना भाजनं यथा॥
en: Persons well read in the scriptures take no notice of the sins that women may commit at heart. Whatever their sins may be they are cleaned by their menstrual course like a metallic plate that is cleansed with ashes.

sa: अपास्य राजधानी वा तरेद् द्रव्येण चापदम्। तद्भावयुक्तो द्रव्याणि जीवन् पुनरुपार्जयेत्॥
en: If the invader be reluctant to make peace, the king should then leave his very capital and all his properties for escaping from danger. If he can save his life he may expect to make similar acquisitions in future.

sa: संयुक्तात्मा समरेष्वाततायी शस्त्रैश्छिन्नो दस्युभिर्वध्यमानः। अश्वग्रीवः कर्मशीलो महात्मा संसिद्धार्थो मोदते स्वर्गलोके॥
en: Wounded by robbers with weapons, bravely fighting with them, and giving up his life in battle, the great Hayagriva, ever devoted to his royal duties, achieved the object of his life and is now enjoying great bliss in heaven.

sa: राज्ञां पूज्यतमो नान्यो यथा धर्मः प्रदर्शितः। ब्रह्मणा लोकरक्षार्थं स्वधर्मस्थापनाय च॥
en: There is nothing which deserves greater respect from kings than Punishment by which the ways of Righteousness are marked out. Brahman himself, for the protection of the world and for establishing the duties of different orders, sent down Punishment.

sa: ब्राह्मणानां क्षतत्राणात् ततः क्षत्रिय उच्यते। प्रथिता धर्मतश्चेयं पृथिवी बहुभिः स्मृता॥
en: And because he also healed the wounds of Brahmanas, therefore, he passed by the name of Kshatriya. And because the Earth (during his regime) became celebrated for the practice of virtue, therefore, she passed by the name of Prithivi.

sa: आततायी हि यो हन्यादाततायिनमागतम्। न तेन भ्रूणहा स स्यान्मन्युस्तं मन्युमार्छति॥
en: He who takes up a weapon and kills an arined enemy advancing against him, does not incur the sin of killing a man, for it is the anger of the advancing enemy that excites the anger of the destroyer.

sa: संजयोऽपि सुतं प्राप्य देवराजसमद्युतिम्। हृष्टः सान्तःपुरो राजा वननित्यो बभूव ह॥
en: Srinjaya, meanwhile, having obtained that child who was effulgent like Indra himself, became filled with joy. The king, accompanied by his wives, and the other ladies of his household, took up his quarter in the midst of a forest.

sa: क्षुधित: कलुषं यातो नास्ति हीरशनार्थिनः। क्षुच्च मां दूषयत्यत्र हरिष्यामि श्वजाघनीम्॥
en: Being hungry I have become sinful. One who seeks food has no shame. It is hunger which is actuating me to commit this sin. It is for this that I wish to take away that haunch of dog's meat.

sa: जीवितं मरणं चैव नाभिनन्दन्न च द्विषन्। वास्यैकं तक्षतो बाहुं चन्दनेनैकमुक्षतः॥
en: I shall not show any liking for life or dislike for death. If one cuts off one arm of mine and another smears the other with sandal-paste, I shall not wish evil to the one or good to other.

sa: सूर्येणाभ्युदितो यश्च ब्रह्मचारी भवत्युत। तथा सूर्याभिनिर्मुक्तः कुनखी श्यावदन्नपि॥ परिवित्तिः परिवेत्ता ब्रह्मघ्नो यश्च कुत्सकः। दिधिषूपपतिर्यः स्यादग्रेदिधिषुरेव च॥ अवकीर्णी भवेद् यश्च द्विजातिवधकस्तथा। अतीर्थे ब्राह्मणस्त्यागी तीर्थे चाप्रतिपादकः॥ ग्रामघाती च कौन्तेय मांसस्य परिविक्रयी। यश्चाग्नीनपविध्येत तथैव ब्रह्मविक्रयी॥ स्त्रीशूद्रवधको यश्च पूर्वः पूर्वस्तु गर्हितः। यथा पशुसमालम्भी गृहदाहस्य कारकः॥ अनृतेनोपवर्ती च प्रतिरोद्धा गुरोस्तथा। एतान्येनांसि सर्वाणि व्युत्क्रान्तसमयश्च यः॥
en: The Brahmacharin, who rises from bed after the sun rise, or goes to bed while the sun is setting, one who has a rotten nail or black tecth, one whose younger brother married first, one who marries before his elder brother is married, one who has been guilty of Brahmanicide, one who speaks ill of others, one who marries a younger sister before the elder sister has been married, one who marries an elder sister after having married a younger one, one who does not observe his vow, one kill who a saint, one who imparts a knowledge of the Vedas to a unworthy person, one who does not impart a knowledge thereof a worthy person, one who takes many lives, one who sells flesh, one who has abandoned his (sacred) fire, one who sells the knowledge of the Vedas, one who kills his preceptor or a woman, on

sa: अथैनमभिनिन्दन्ति भिन्नं कुम्भमिवाश्मनि। तस्माद् धर्मेण विजयं कोशं लिप्सेत भूमिपः॥
en: Then seeing him look like an earthen pot broken on a stone surface, people describe him as he deserves. The king should, therefore, seek both victory and the increment of his resources, by fair means.

sa: यथा शल्यकवानाखुः पदं धूनयते सदा। अतीक्ष्णेनाभ्युपायेन तथा राष्ट्र समापिबेत्॥
en: He should behave like a mouse which although has got sharp and pointed teeth yet cuts the feet of sleeping animals in such a way that they do not at all become conscious of it.

sa: तस्य संदृश्य सद्भावमुपविश्स्य धीमतः। सर्वे सत्त्वाः समीपस्था भवन्ति वनचारिणः॥
en: Highly intelligent, as he was, as he sat on his seat, the goodness of his conduct having been known to all the creatures that dwelt in that forest, they used to approach him with affection.

sa: अशङ्कयमपि शङ्केत नित्यं शङ्केत शङ्कितात्। भयं ह्यशङ्कितात्जातं समूलमपि कृन्तति॥
en: The king should fear him from whom there is no fear; he should also always fear them who should be feared. Fear rising from a person who is not feared, may bring on total extermination.

sa: ब्रह्मणश्च प्रणाशेन धर्मो व्यनशदीश्वर। ततः स्म समतां याता मत्यस्त्रिभुवनेश्व॥
en: With the loss of the Vedas, o Supreme Lord, righteousness also has been lost. For this, O Supreme Lord of the three worlds, we are about to be reduced to the status of human beings.

sa: व्यक्तश्चानुग्रहो यस्य यथार्थश्चापि निग्रहः। गुप्तात्मा गुप्तराष्ट्रश्च स राजा राजधर्मवित्॥
en: That king is a master of his royal duties who rewards his officers and subjects publicly, who punishes those who deserve punishment, who protects his own self, and who protects his kingdom from very evil.

sa: देववंशान् ब्रह्मवंशान् पितृवंशांश्च शाश्वतान्। संविभज्य गुरोश्चर्यां तद् वै दुष्करमुच्यते॥
en: The proper performance of these eternal duties, viz., the worship of the gods, the study of the Vedas, and the gratification of the Pitris, as also respectful services to the preceptor,-is the austerest of penances.

sa: अनीकं ये विभिन्दन्ति भिन्न संस्थापयन्ति च। समानाशनपानास्ते कार्याः द्विगुणवेतनाः॥
en: Those of your warriors who break the ranks of enemies, or rally your retreating soldiers, should have their pay doubled and should be honoured by you with food, drink, and seats equal to your own.

sa: राजानं शतधन्वानं दिलीपं सत्यवादिनम्। येऽपश्यन् सुमहात्मानं तेऽपि स्वर्गजितो नराः॥
en: Those men went to heaven who could obtain a glance even of the great king Dwilipa who was ever truthful in speech and whose bow could bear a hundred enemies powerful like a hundred Anantas.

sa: न पक्षिणो बभ्रमुरन्तरिक्षे तदा महास्त्रेण कृतेऽन्धकारे॥ रुवाह दिव्यः सुरभिस्तदानीम्।
en: By those arrows of great swiftness the sky became so dark that even the birds could not take their flights, and gentle and sweet-scented wind began to blow, as if sent by the Heavenly father.

sa: नष्टचन्द्रा यथा रात्रि: सेनेयं हतनायका। नागभग्नद्रुमा शुष्का नदीवाकुलतां गता॥
en: This army of yours that is now without a leader is like a night without the Moon or like a river that is dried up with all the trees on its banks broken by elephants.

sa: यस्तु संसहते तानि भर्तुः प्रियचिकीर्षया। समानसुखदुःखं तं पृच्छेदर्थेषु मानवम्॥
en: That one, amongst them, who subdues his anger from desire of doing good to his master,-that person who partakes in the king's happiness and misfortune, should be consulted by the king in all his affairs.

sa: येऽस्मान्न प्रतिगृह्णन्ति दस्युभोजनशङ्कया। तेषामासज्य गेहेषु कल्य एव स गच्छति॥
en: As regards those who were reluctant, from fear of others, to accept gifts from him for the profession he followed, he used to repair to their houses before dawn and leave meat at their doors.

sa: नैवास्य कश्चिद् भविता नायं भवति कस्यचित्। पथि सङ्गतमेवेदं दारबन्धुसुहृज्जनैः॥
en: No one can become any one's own, nor can any one become anybody else's own. Our union here with wives and kinsmen and wellwishers is like that of travellers at an inn in the road.

sa: तदेव विस्तरेणोक्तः पूर्वदृष्टं सतां मतम्। प्रणेयं राजधर्माणां प्रब्रूहि भरतर्षभ॥
en: You have, indeed, described fully those duties as approved by the wise. Do you, however, O foremost of Bharata's race give us an abridgement of the same, so that we may keep it in memory.

sa: प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्। न तप्येदर्थकृच्छ्रेषु प्रजाहितमनुस्मरन्॥
en: Do not be overjoyed when anything pleasant occurs, nor give away to sorrow when anything disagreeable occurs. Never grieve when your wealth is exhausted, and always remember the duty of doing good to your subjects.

sa: एकान्तशीली विमृशन् पक्वापक्वेन वर्तयन्। पितृन् देवांश्च वन्येन वाग्भिरद्भिश्च तर्पयन्॥
en: Leading a retired life and engaged in contemplation, I shall live upon ripe and unripe fruits and propitiate the departed manes and the gods with offerings of forest fruits and spring water and beautiful hymns.

sa: तां पश्य रुदतीमार्ता मुक्तकेशीमधोमुखीम्। हतं पतिमुपासन्ती द्रोणं शस्त्रभृतां वरम्॥
en: Look at that sorrow-stricken lady, fallen upon the Earth, with disheveled hair and face Juser hanging down. Alas, she serves sorrowfully her lifeless husband, that best of all holders of weapons, lying on the ground.

sa: अपशास्त्रपरो राजा धर्मार्थान्नाधिगच्छति। अस्थाने चास्य तद् वित्तं सर्वमेव विनश्यति॥
en: That king, who is negligent about the means of acquiring riches, never succeeds in acquiring both religious merit and wealth. The wealth again that he acquires (by such means) is spent lavishly on unworthy objects.

sa: स्वाध्याययज्ञसंसिद्धा दृश्यन्ते बहवो जनाः। तपोरताश्च मुनयो येषां लोकाः सनातनाः॥
en: This however, is not true. Many persons are scen who have become successful through Sacrifice in the shape of Vedic study. Many sages are seen who by practising penances have acquired eternal regions for themselves.

sa: क्रीडितुं तेन चेच्छन्ति ससूत्रेणेव पक्षिणा। अस्मत्प्रणेयो राजेति लोकांश्चैव वदन्त्युत॥
en: They wish to sport with the king as with a bird tied in a rope, and always make the people understand that the king is on very intimate terms with them and loves them dearly.

sa: भीतवत् संविधातव्यं यावद् भयमनागतम्। आगतं तु भयं दृष्ट्वा प्रहर्तव्यमभीतवत्॥
en: As long as the cause of fear does not actually arrive, the king should make all his arrangements like a person filled with fear. When, however, the cause of fear arrives, he should smite fearlessly.

sa: उद्गाताऽत्र पुनर्भीमः प्रस्तोता सुमहाबलः। विनदन् स नरव्याघ्रो नागानीकान्तकृद् रणे॥
en: The repeater (Udgatri) of those incantations again will be Bhima, who will also be the Prastori (the prepare), that foremost of men, that destroyer of the elephants in the army, making loud roars in battle.

sa: यथा रथास्तथा नागा बद्धकक्षाः स्वलंकृताः। बभूवुः सप्तपुरुषा रत्नवन्त इवाद्रयः॥
en: As the chariots had bells and wreaths of pearls and other ornaments so had the elephants and on the back of each were mounted seven men making the animals look like hills decks with jewels.

sa: निश्चितं धार्तराष्ट्राणां सकर्णानां जनार्दन। भीष्मद्रोणमुखान् पार्था न शक्ताः प्रतिवीक्षितुम्॥
en: It is the conviction of the sons of Dhritarashtra and of Karna, O Janardana, that the sons of Pritha are not capable of even gazing at an army under the leadership of Bhishma and Drona.

sa: एतामवस्थां प्राप्यैके मरणं वविरे जनाः। ग्रामायके वनायके नाशायैके प्रवव्रजुः॥
en: Having reached this condition (i.e. poverty) one class of men prefer death; another retire to villages (form cities); a third to the wilderness; while the fourth rove about with a view to meet speedy death.

sa: यदाह भरतश्रेष्ठो भीष्मस्तत् क्रियतां नृप। न काममर्थलिप्सूनां वचनं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: What the chief among the race of Bharata, Bhishma, has said-do that, O protector of men. It is not proper that you should do what they that covet desire and wealth tell you to do.

sa: अस्मॅिल्लोके तपस्तप्तं फलमन्यत्र भुज्यते। ब्राह्मणानामिमे लोका धात्वे तपसि तिष्ठताम्॥
en: The fruits of asceticism in this world are enjoyed in the other (by those who have not brought their souls under their control); but to those blessed persons engaged in austerities these regions yield fruits.

sa: ते वा युधि दुराधर्षा भवन्त्वेकस्य सैनिकाः। अयुध्यमानः संग्रामे न्यस्तशस्त्रोऽहमेकतः॥
en: Let them, who are hard to vanquish in battle, be the army of one party of you and let myself who shall not fight, having put off my weapons, take the side of the other.

sa: अथान्तरिक्षे वागासीद् दिव्यरूपा मनोरमा। सहस्राक्षसमः कुन्ति भविष्यत्येष ते सुतः॥
en: There was heard a voice in the sky which seemed to be celestial and which pleased the heart; it said: 0 Kunti, this son of yours will be equal to him of a thousand eyes.

sa: यत्र मन्येत भूयिष्ठं प्रावृषीव तृणोपलम्। अन्नं पानं ब्राह्मणस्य तज्जीवेन्नानुसंज्वरेत्॥
en: Whenever (in whatever family) food and drink fit for a Brahmana abound like grass and reeds in the spots, there should (a Yogi) go for his living and not pain himself (by hunger and thirst).

sa: श्लाध्यः पार्थिववंशस्य प्रमुखे वाहिनीपतिः। पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृतः शतशाख इव द्रुमः॥
en: He who is enviable in the races of the rulers of the earth, the foremost of all leaders of armies and who surrounded by sons and grandsons is like a tree with a hundred branches,

sa: ततोऽस्य समये जज्ञे पुत्रो बालरविप्रभः। शिबिर्नाम्नाभिविख्यातो यः स पार्थिवसत्तमः॥
en: Then was born to him in due time a son who was a boy similar in effulgence to the sun; he lived to be an excellent ruler of the earth known by the name Shivi.

sa: आप्नुमाप्तं तथापीदमविनीतेन सर्वथा। त्वं ह्योवात्र भृशं ग. धृतराष्ट्र सुतप्रियः॥
en: But notwithstanding all this, Duryodhana, having to humility in him, has obtained what is unobtainable by all means and you, O Dhritarashtra, are very much blamable for this, for you are fond of your son.

sa: वासुदेव उवाच उपासितास्ते राधेय ब्राह्मण वेदपारगाः। तत्त्वार्थं परिपृष्टाश्च नियतेनानसूयया।॥
en: Vasudeva said Many Brahmanas conversant with the Vedas have been worshipped by you, O son of Radha and they have also been asked about truth by you with your mind attentive and free from jealousy.

sa: करजैरतुदंश्चान्ये विहाय भयमुत्तमम्। बहुधा युध्यमानास्ते युद्धमार्गः प्लवङ्गमाः॥ नानाप्रहरणैर्भीमै राक्षसेन्द्रमताडयन्।
en: (And) giving up their fear some began to tear him with nails and several monkeys fought him by resorting to various ways (of battle). And they hurled at that foremost of Rakshasas various terrible weapons.

sa: धर्मादर्थात् सुखाच्चैव मा राजन् नीनशः प्रजाः। नर्थमर्थं मन्वानोऽप्यर्थं नर्थमात्मनः॥
en: Do not, O king, destroy these beings of the birth for the sake of vice and earthy good for the sake of happiness thinking evil to be good and good to be evil for yourself.

sa: कर्मणा क्षत्रियाश्चैते निघृणा भोगिभोजिनः। ज्ञातिसंक्षयकर्तृत्वाद् ब्राह्मण्यं न लभन्ति वै॥
en: By their habits of life they are Kshatriyas; but as they live on snakes, they are without humanity; and owing to their constant warfare with their kinsmen they never attain to the region of Brahma.

sa: राजपिण्डभयादेते यदि हास्यन्ति जीवितम्। न हि शक्ष्यन्ति राजानं युधिष्ठिरमुदीक्षितुम्॥
en: If foe the fear of losing the maintenance they get from the king, they can think lightly of their very lives, they will yet not be able to see the king Yudhishthira with (angry) eyes.

sa: क्षीणः सर्वार्थहीनश्च निर्घातिबन्धुवर्जितः। को दिशं प्रतिपत्स्यामि दीनः शत्रुवशं गतः॥
en: Now I am weak, destitute of all resources and deprived of all kinsmen and left my friends and also I am poor and possessed by my foes-To what point of the horizon shall I depart?

sa: तत्र नादो महानासीत् पाण्डवानां विशाम्पते॥ सौबलं समरे दृष्ट्वा विचरन्तमभीतवत्।
en: On the very sight of the son of Subala, who was wandering about of in the field of battle most fearlessly, there had taken place, O ruler of earth, great roar amongst the Pandava host.

sa: स्त्वप्रेषितैर्लोहिताङ्गैर्रिहहै। शेते स पापः सुविभिन्नगात्रः कच्चिद् भग्नौ धार्तराष्ट्रस्य बाहू॥
en: Does the scoundrel lie low on the battlefield today being mangled all over the body with long-ranging blood-besmeared shafts hurled by you from your bow. Could you break in twin the arms of Dhritarashtra's sons?

sa: ततो घोरं महाराज अस्त्रयुद्धमवर्तत॥ ग्रहयुद्धं यथां घोरं प्रजासंहरणे ह्यभूत।
en: Then, O mighty king, there ensued a very dreadful battle of weapons, even as there had taken place a very terrible battle of the planets, during the time of destruction of creatures of the universe.

sa: स्वमनीकमवस्थाप्य बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः। युद्ध्वा च सुचिरं कालं पाण्डवैः सह भारत॥
en: Then with the confidence in the strength of his own arms, having arranged his own army in a regular position and O descendant of the Bharata race, having fought for a while with the Pandavas.

sa: जहि तूबरकं क्षिप्रं कर्णस्य बलमादधत्। एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा तव पुत्रं तवात्मजः॥
en: Thus spoken to, your son Durjaya bowed assent to the words of your royal son saying 'So be it then;' and then he rushed at Bhimasena engaged with Karna, covering the former with his arrows.

sa: प्रजहुः सैन्धवं भीता द्वौ समं नाप्यधावताम्॥ तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम कुन्तीपुत्रस्य विक्रमम्।
en: Where greatly frightened frightened and they abandoned the ruler of the Sindhus. They were so much confused that no two persons were seen to fly together. Then we beheld the wonderful prowess of Kunti's son.

sa: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु रथादाप्लुत्य भारत। शक्तिं चिक्षेप चित्राय स्वर्णदण्डामलंकृताम्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, he (Prativindhya), in the mean time, having descended from his car, threw at Chitra the arrow, called Shakti, that was furnished with golden balls and decked with several ornaments.

sa: सात्यकिस्तु रणे द्रोणं राजन् विव्याध सप्तभिः। हेमपुङ्खैः शिलाधौतैः कङ्कबर्हिणवाजितैः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, Satyaki in that battle, pierced Drona with seven arrows whetted on stone and furnished with golden wings as well as with wings made of the feathers of the Kanka and the peacock.

sa: त्वत्कृते ह्यहमद्राक्षं दह्यमानां वरूथिनीम्। सहस्रशः शरैर्मुक्तैः पाण्डवेन वृषेण च॥
en: It was through your fault that I had to see our army consumed in thousands by the shafts discharged by Pandu's son and by Vrisha. numerous other mighty car-warriors and your other sons have fallen.

sa: सिन्धुरावधेनेमे घटोत्कचवधेन ते। अमर्षिताः सुसंक्रुद्धा रणं चक्रुः कथं निशि॥
en: How indeed did those, worked up with anger at the death of the ruler of the Sindhus and those at the death of Ghatotkacha, each side unable to brook their loss, fight during that night.

sa: निहताः पुरुषेन्द्रेणर तचापि विदितं तव। गन्धर्वा घोषयात्रायां चित्रसेनादयो जिताः॥
en: Proud of their strength, were then slain by that foremost of men. This also you know. On the occasion of the numbering of cattle, the Gandharvas, headed by Chitrasena and others, were defeated by him.

sa: जलसंधार्णवं तीा काम्बोजानां च वाहिनीम्। हार्दिक्यमकरान्मुक्तं तीर्णे वै सैन्यसागरम्॥
en: After he had passed through the son of Jalasandha's troops, as also the host of the Kamboja, after had escaped the alligator constituted by Hridika's son, after he had forded through that ocean like host.

sa: तेषां ज्यातलनिर्घोषो रथनेमिस्वनश्च ह। मेघानामिव धर्मान्ते बभूव तुमुलो निशि॥
en: In that night the sound of their palms and the twang of their bow-strings and the clatter of their car-wheels were so loud as to resemble and rumble of cloud at the end of summer.

sa: तस्मिन् सोमाग्निविष्णूनां क्षोभेण ब्रह्मरुद्रयोः। स रथो धनुषः क्षोभादतीव ह्यवसीदति॥
en: On account of the pressure of Soma Agni and Vishnu in that shaft and that caused by both Brahman and Rudra, as also of great weight of that formidable bow, that car began to sink.

sa: ततः पराङ्मुखप्रायं निरुत्साहं बलं तव। व्यालम्बत महाराज प्रायशः शस्त्रवेष्टितम्॥
en: O king, your very army, about to fly, being thus slain and surrounded on all sides, with weapons, lost all energy and being greatly confounded, was at their wit's end as to what to do.

sa: रथांश्च बहुधा भग्नान् हेमकिङ्किणिनः शुभान्॥ वाजिनश्च हतान् पश्य निष्कीर्णान्त्राशराहतान्।
en: Look at the beautiful chariots splitted here in pieces in which tiny bells made of gold are fixed. The horses injured by arrows are fell dead there and their intestines have come out from belly.

sa: संजय उवाच काल्यमानेषु सैन्येषु शैनेयेन ततस्ततः। भारद्वाजः शरवातैर्महद्भिः समवाकिरत्॥
en: Sanjaya said When the troops on those parts of the field through which Sini's grandson had passed were compelled by him to tremble, the son of Bharadvaja covered him with a mighty shower of arrows.

sa: गजश्च गिरिसंकाशो गवयश्च महाबलः। गवाक्षश्चाग्रतो यातु गवां दृप्त इवर्षभः॥
en: And let Gaja resembling a hill, and the exceedingly powerful Gavaya, and that monkey, Gavaksa, master of the leaping ones,* like a haughty bull among kine, go in the van of the monkey-host. *i.e. monkeys.

sa: निकुम्भाग्रज वीर्यं ते बाणवेगं तदद्भुतम्॥ संनतिश्च प्रभावश्च तव वा रावणस्य वा। प्रह्लादबलिवृत्रघ्नकुबेरवरुणोपम॥ एकस्त्वमनुजातोऽसि पितरं बलवत्तरम्। त्वामेवैकं महाबाहुं शूलहस्तमरिंदमम्॥ त्रिदशा नातिवर्तन्ते जितेन्द्रियमिवाधयः। विक्रमस्व महाबुद्धे कर्माणि मम पश्य च॥
en: O elder brother of Nikumbha, marvellous are your might and the force of yourself as well as the modesty and prowess that are your and Ravana's. And, o you equal to Prahrada or Vall or the slayer of Vặtra or Varuņa or Kuvera! You alone walk in the wake of you yet mightier father. As mental anguish does not dog one that has controlled his senses, the celestials cannot cope in conflict with you alone, O repressor of foes, O of mighty arms, bearing your dart in your hand. O you of high intelligence, put forth your prowess! and do you also witness my work.

sa: प्रियं जनमपश्यन्तीं पश्यन्तीं राक्षसीगणम्। स्वगणेन मृगी हीनां श्वगणेनावृतामिव ॥
en: Separated from her kith and kin and not beholding Rāma and Lakşmaņa* but the Rāks asīs, she appeared like a hind surrounded by dogs. *Priyājanam-literally means dear ones—but here it refers to Rāma and Lakşmana.

sa: सा प्रकृत्यैव तन्वङ्गी तद्वियोगाच्च कर्शिता। प्रतिपत्पाठशीलस्य विद्येव तनुतां गता॥
en: She has really been greatly reduced and worn out by the separation of her lord. Her person has been shattered like to learning waning by its prosecution on the first day of a lunar fortnight.

sa: स भग्नबाहरुकटीपयोधरः क्षरनसृनिर्मथितास्थिलोचनः। सम्भिन्नसंधिः प्रविकीर्णबन्धनो हतः क्षितौ वायुसुतेन राक्षसः॥
en: And with his arms, thighs and chest crushed, bleeding, (having his bones and eyes smashed, his joints riven, and his tendons snapped, the Rākṣasa lay on the earth, slain by the offspring of the Wind-god.

sa: ऋक्षावानरशार्दूलैर्नखदंष्ट्रायुधैरपि। कराग्रैश्चरणाप्रैश्च वानरैरुद्धतं रजः॥ भीममन्तर्दधे लोकं निवार्य सवितुः प्रभाम्।
en: The mighty dust raised by bears, monkeys, and tigers, having for their weapons nails and teeth, with the foreparts of their feet and hands, enveloped the world, and the splendour of the sun was obscured.

sa: ततो हरीणां तदनीकमुग्रं रराज शैलोद्यतवृक्षहस्तम्। गिरेः समीपानुगतं यथैव महन्महाम्भोधरजालमुग्रम्॥
en: Then that dreadful army of monkeys, upraising crags and holding trees in their hands, appeared like mighty masses of scowling clouds bordering a mountain.* *This is apt, seeing that Larika was situated on a hill.

sa: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महाथ रघुप्रवीरः प्लवगर्षभैर्वृतः। स्तदा महात्मा त्वरितं निरीक्षते।४३॥
en: Having said these words pregnant with a high significance, the high-souled and heroic descendant of Raghu, being surrounded by monkeys, began to concert various plans for the destruction of that terrible Raksasa of wicked deeds.

sa: ते राघवधनुर्मुक्ता रुक्मपुङ्खाः शिखिप्रभाः। सुपर्णाः काञ्चना भूत्वा विचेरुः सर्पशत्रवः॥
en: Discharged from Rāghava's bow, those arrows plated with gold at the feathered parts and furnished with the splendour of peacocks, becoming golden birds-began to range (the field of battle) as the enemies of the serpents.

sa: मित्रभावेन संप्राप्तं न त्यजेयं कथंचन। दोषो यद्यपि तस्य स्यात्सतामेतदगर्हितम्॥
en: (Vibhīşaņa) has come here as friend so I cannot forsake him by any means. And even if he has come with any evil intent it is not culpable for the pious to afford him shelter.

sa: पुत्रि प्रदानकालोऽयं यौवन व्यतिवर्तते। प्रत्याख्यानाच्च भीतैस्त्वं न वरैः परिगृह्यसे॥
en: O daughter, the time has come when I should give you away. Your youth is about to be passed. (Kept back) by the fear of refusal, no suiter has sought you (up to his time).

sa: स तं गृहीत्वानिलतुल्यवेगं सविस्फुलिङ्गज्वलनप्रकाशम्। बाणं महेन्द्राशनितुल्यवेगं चिक्षेप सुग्रीववधाय रुष्टः॥
en: Taking that shaft endowed with the vehemence of the wind, flaming like a fire aglow, and having the impetuosity of the great Indra's thunder-bolt, (Ravana) hurled it in rage to compass the destruction of Sugrīva.

sa: विजयेत महीं राजा प्रवासी स्वस्तिमान्भवेत्॥ स्त्रियो रजस्वलाः श्रुत्वा पुत्रान्सूयुरनुत्तमान्।
en: Hearing this a king may conquer the earth, and one living in a foreign country fare well. If a female, during her monthly course, hears the story, she shall give birth to an excellent son.

sa: तस्मिन्हते भ्रातरि रावणस्य तनैर्ऋतानां बलमर्णवाभम्। त्यक्तायुधं केवलजीवितार्थ दुद्राव भिन्नार्णवसंनिकाशम्॥
en: On that brother of Rāvaņa having been slain, that host of Nairtas appearing like the ocean in grandeur, leaving its arms behind, solely for life rushed away, like to the deep riven (by the winds).

sa: तेन नादेन महता चैत्यपालाः शतं ययुः। गृहीत्वा विविधानस्त्रान्प्रासान्खङ्गान् परश्वधान्॥
en: In consequence of that mighty cry, an hundred guards attached to the Caitya sallied out, taking various weapons-bearded darts, scimitars and axes; and they surrounded the Wind-god's offspring, as he went on increasing his body.

sa: या मे प्रीतिः पुष्कराक्ष त्वदर्शनसमुद्भवा। सा किमाख्यायते तुभ्यमन्तरात्मासि देहिनाम्॥
en: He said-'The joy I feel at the sight of yourself, who have come here, O you with lotus eyes, what is the use of describing? For, you are the inner soul of all corporeal beings.'

sa: नकुलात् पूर्वजं पार्थं न पश्याम्यमितौजसम्। अजेयमुग्रधन्वानं तेन तप्ये वृकोदर॥
en: O Vrikodara, I do not see the immediate elder of Nakula, the immeasurably powerful Partha (Arjuna) who is invincible and who is the wielder of the strongest bow. For this, O Vrikodara, I am miserable.

sa: वनस्पतिं च यो हन्यादमावास्यामबुद्धिमान्। अपि टेकेन पत्रेण लिप्यते ब्रह्महत्यया।॥
en: That man of little understanding who cuts down a large tree on the day of the new moon, becomes sullied with the sin of Brahmanicide. By killing even a single leaf one commits that sin.

sa: एतत् प्रब्रूहि भगवन् मया पृष्टो यथातथम्। श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वेन सर्वमेतन्महामुने॥
en: O you possessor of the six qualities the Bhagas, explain to me all this truly as I have questioned you on the matter. O great sage, I want to hear the truth about the subject.
